Resolved against the generator spec, which is the source of truth for placement: board_b_spec.py NETS puts C11.2 on '/DC-DC Conversion/-13.5V OUT' and C3.1 on '/DC-DC Conversion/+13.5V OUT'. That matches the board-b doc's U4 net table, the locked baseline, and the sheet-geometry adjacency probe recorded in BB-12; inventory.json's function text was the lone outlier and is corrected. The 11.5 V margin is unaffected -- it was already computed against a 13.5 V magnitude, which both rails share.

The manufacturer RATING is now fully sourced: 240 mA rms @120Hz/105C with a x1.30 multiplier at 10kHz and above, giving 312 mA rms at the project's 150kHz switching frequency, and max ESR ~0.51 Ohm derived from the specified tan-delta. The earlier partial-extraction figures (approx. 1.0A ripple, approx. 0.035 Ohm ESR) were wrong by ~4x and ~14x respectively, both in the non-conservative direction, and have been superseded. The domain stays OPEN because applying the rating shows a problem rather than clearing one. C24's line now carries ripple and ESR facts too (fact-c22387780-ripple-hf-derate, fact-c22387780-esr-120hz), so the C11 || C24 split the review could not bound is now computable: splitting the review's ~0.77 A by the two parts' max-ESR ratio originally gave C11 ~362 mA against its 312 mA rating (~1.16x over) and C24 ~408 mA against 403 mA (~1.01x). The C11 || C24 exceedance is resolved by resize: decision neg-rail-cap-bank adds C12 (a second C22387780) in parallel, putting C11 at ~237 mA = 75.9% of its 312 mA rating in the three-can split (fact-c2983319-c11-ripple-share-3can). C3 is far less exposed -- a buck output cap carries only inductor ripple, not the pulsating diode current C11 sees. Needs a bench measurement -- issue #155, BB-7.

The manufacturer datasheet states the case size three independent ways on page 1 -- the header line 'GVT, 25v, 470uF, 8x10.5', the Description line 'D8H10.5mm', and the Dimension & Marking table Case row 'Phi 8x10.5' with A 8.3 / B 8.3 / C 9.0 / D 8.0 / P 3.1 / L 10.5. Those map digit-for-digit onto zudo-pd:CAP-SMD_BD8.0-L8.3-W8.3-LS9.0-FD, which is now the assigned land. This closes issue #150: the part is Phi 8, not Phi 10, so no design decision was required -- the previous BD10.0 assignment was simply wrong.
